themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 4.95)—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, new vending activity, or resident frustration with street commerce in Sheepshead Bay.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 per week 8-week baseline
No prior Reddit or local news mentions indicating this was anticipated
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and residents: Is enforcement ramping up, or is illegal vending increasing? Who initiated the complaints?
Check with DSNY and DOE enforcement divisions on whether there's a new operation targeting CD 315 this week

themes_detail.label: Building Inspection Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a 1.1 per week average—a 256% spike (z-score: 3.68)—potentially signaling widespread code violations, tenant disputes, or a concentrated inspection campaign in the district.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 per week 8-week baseline
585 total building permits filed in last 90 days (360 alterations), suggesting active construction and renovation activity that may be triggering inspections
reporting_angles: Identify which properties triggered SPIT complaints and why—are they construction sites, residential buildings with habitability issues, or illegal conversions?
Interview tenants and property managers: Are inspections responding to complaints, or proactively enforcing new code violations?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branch Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged to 14 LAST WEEK versus a 3.6 per week baseline—a 286% spike (z-score: 6.58)—suggesting storm damage, deferred maintenance, or safety hazards in parks and streets across the district.
evidence: 14 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 per week 8-week baseline
Clustered with Maintenance or Facility complaints (9 LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 baseline, +243%), suggesting broader infrastructure backlog
reporting_angles: Was there recent weather (storms, high winds) that downed or weakened branches, or is this a deferred maintenance problem?
Map the 14 complaints: Are they concentrated in specific parks or streets, or distributed across the district?

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking & Sanitation Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Drinking complaints hit 4 LAST WEEK from a nearly nonexistent baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66, highest severity)—possibly indicating emerging public alcohol consumption issues or a change in enforcement/reporting patterns.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 per week 8-week baseline
1500% spike with z-score of 8.66 (highest statistical severity in dataset)
Clustered with smoking/vaping spike (6 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.0 baseline, +500%) and litter basket complaints (3 last week vs. 0.2 baseline, +1100%)
reporting_angles: Identify where the 4 drinking complaints originated (parks, beaches, commercial areas) and whether they involve homelessness, nightlife zones, or new enforcement
Interview NYPD and Parks Enforcement Patrol: Is this a real behavioral shift or a reporting artifact?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages (Delayed Signal)
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked to 4 three weeks ago from a 0.4 per week baseline—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—but signal is aging; still worth tracking whether outages persist in aging residential buildings, especially amid active alteration work (360 permits filed).
evidence: 4 elevator complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 per week 8-week baseline
360 alteration permits filed in last 90 days may have disrupted elevator maintenance or service in residential buildings
reporting_angles: Follow up: Are elevator complaints still elevated THIS WEEK, or has the spike resolved? Check current 311 data.
Investigate whether construction alteration permits are delaying elevator repairs or inspections in residential buildings
